newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa spikes higher on weaker stg.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa spikes higher on weaker stg.

text.p: Cocoa futures shot higher on Monday in an afternoon wave of trade short-covering buoyed by weaker sterling.
"It's all currency-based," said one trader. "There are no fundamental news."
Benchmark September was driven to 1,020 stg a tonne -the highest level in a week- as it regained a foothold above the 1,000 stg, previously a heavy resistance.
After filling in a small chart gap at 1,012-1,015, it stalled at 1,020, seen as the next barrier, before finishing at 1,018, still a hefty 26 stg gain on the day.
Volume at 5,083 lots was modest. Sept/Dec spread stood at 35 stg against 38 on Friday.
Traders said cocoa's run-up came on the back of sterling's fall against the dollar and German mark.
Sterling hovered at above 3.01 marks after shedding five pfennigs - or almost two percent - during European session in a wave of profit-taking.
The broad dollar strength also added pressure on sterling. The sterling probed six-week lows of just shy of $1.63. It traded around $1.66 last week.
After the immediate 1,020, the next upside target is the July 11 high of 1,053. On the downside, the 1,000 level becomes the immediate support, followed by 965.

In other news, industry analysts said Ivorian cocoa grind could rise to around 200,000 tonnes in the 1997/98 season (Oct-Sept) from an estimated 145,000 tonnes in 1996/97 as new capacity comes on stream.
